topic: Explicitly Defaulting and Deleting Special Member Functions: Impact on Compiler Optimization and Memory Layout
explanation: This concept delves into the intricate details of how compilers handle special member functions (constructors, destructors, assignment operators, etc.) when explicitly defaulted or deleted.  Understanding this allows for fine-grained control over object lifetime, memory management, and optimization opportunities.  Explicitly defining these functions, even as defaults, can drastically affect compiler optimization strategies compared to relying on implicit generation.  Deleted functions prevent unwanted object creation or copying, leading to improved type safety and potentially reduced code bloat.  The compiler's ability to perform return value optimization (RVO) and copy elision is significantly affected by the presence and nature of these functions.
